barriers.description: The participant samples were skewed toward higher-educated, Dutch-background parents, limiting access to diverse user perspectives (eg, low-SES or non-Dutch backgrounds).
barriers.justification: This recruitment/sampling limitation constrained the designers' ability to manage user understanding and facilitate involvement from underrepresented groups, reducing confidence that insights reflected the full target population and hindering context-of-use understanding.
barriers.reference_excerpt: The participants were female parents... Most participants were higher educated (21/26, 81%) and had a Dutch background (23/26, 88%). A final evaluation was aimed at also assessing a fit with people with lower health literacy skills given that the convenience sample did particularly comprise people with higher education.

barriers.description: Initial interactive choices in the prototype were too obvious, producing a tendency toward the 'right choice' and preventing users from learning through making mistakes.
barriers.justification: This design flaw limited the team's ability to evaluate how parents learn from the intervention and to integrate realistic feedback into iterations, thereby hindering evaluation of designs and iterative refinement workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: However, the options of parenting reactions that users could choose were declared to be too obvious, with the user experiencing a tendency toward the "right choice." This implied that the user did not have the full opportunity to learn from their mistakes as they were not provided with information on why a certain choice may be less adequate.
